sources.notes: The page lists Asian nationalities requiring prior approval and separately warns about restricted travel documents; it does not establish the complete visa outcome for the target passports.

sources.title: E Applications for Visa and Residence Permits
sources.notes: The official service page says visa applications are for foreigners who do not need prior approval, must be submitted from outside Jordan, and lists official fee options; the public page does not expose a target-passport-specific final result.

sources.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Türkiye
sources.title: Visa Information For Foreigners
sources.notes: The official country-by-country table directly distinguishes PRC ordinary passports, Hong Kong SAR passports and Macao SAR passports, including different exemption periods.

sources.authority: Ministry of Interior, Arab Republic of Egypt
sources.title: Egypt Electronic Visa Portal — FAQ eligibility list
sources.notes: The official FAQ eligibility panel lists China among nationalities that can apply for an Egyptian e-Visa; Hong Kong and Macao are not displayed in the reviewed list, which is not treated as a complete entry-ban conclusion.

sources.title: Countries and regions requiring a visa to travel to Mexico
sources.notes: The official page states that nationals of listed countries must obtain a visa under any entry condition; the attached official list includes China and the page describes the visitor route for tourism and other unpaid activities.

sources.authority: Consulate General of Mexico in Hong Kong
sources.title: Mexican Visa Exemptions
sources.notes: The official consular page directly states that Hong Kong and Macao passport holders do not require a visa for tourism, transit or business stays up to 90 days.

sources.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Brazil
sources.title: Visa requirements by country — list of countries
sources.notes: The official country entry for China states that diplomatic and official passport holders are exempt under the stated conditions, while all other passport types require a visa before entering Brazil.

sources.authority: Consulate General of Brazil in Hong Kong, Ministry of Foreign Affairs
sources.title: Tourist Visa
sources.notes: The official consular page states that Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR passport holders are exempt from Visitor Visa for tourism, transit or business stays up to 90 days, while Hong Kong SAR Document of Identity and Macao Travel Permit holders require an entry visa.

sources.authority: Consulate General of Peru in London, Ministry of Foreign Affairs
sources.title: Tourism Visas
sources.notes: The official consular page lists Hong Kong among Asian nationalities not requiring a tourist visa and states that Chinese nationals may enter visa-free only with a qualifying UK, Canada, Australia, Schengen or US visa valid for at least six months at entry; Macao is not displayed in the reviewed list.

sources.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Colombia
sources.title: Entry to Colombia and Courtesy Visa Information
sources.notes: The official entry-information PDF lists Hong Kong SAR as a special territory exempt from the Visitor (V) visa for short stays, states that Chinese nationals need a US or Schengen permanent residence permit or visa valid for more than six months to use the conditional exemption, and directs those who do not meet the conditions to obtain a visa; Macao is not listed in the reviewed special-territory section.

sources.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Chile, Consular Services
sources.title: Visas para ingresar a Chile
sources.notes: The official consular selector returns China as visa required with a six-month Canada/United States visa or Green Card exception, Hong Kong as visa exempt for 90 days, and Macao as visa exempt for 30 days; the page also defines the transitory stay route as up to 90 days and exposes official notes for each country row.

sources.title: Regimen de Visas
sources.notes: The official migration table marks REPUBLICA POPULAR CHINA as REQUIERE VISA for Pasaporte Ordinario (Turista), with HABILITADO in the Visa EEUU and Green CARD columns; HONG KONG (REPUBLICA CHINA) and MACAO (REPUBLICA CHINA) have no ordinary-tourist REQUIERE VISA marker. The page does not provide a stay period for the no-visa rows.

sources.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Uruguay, Consulate General in Hong Kong
sources.title: Visas
sources.notes: The official consular page provides tourist-visa requirements and directs applicants to consult the Uruguayan Ministry of the Interior's Visa Policy for Foreign Nationals before applying, but the reviewed page does not expose a target-passport-specific China, Hong Kong or Macao outcome.

sources.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Human Mobility of Ecuador
sources.title: Lista de países que deben presentar visa al ingresar al Ecuador
sources.notes: The official entry-visa list includes República Popular China among nationalities that must present a visa to enter Ecuador; it does not separately identify Hong Kong or Macao SAR passports.

sources.authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Human Mobility of Ecuador
sources.title: Acuerdo Ministerial No. 0000064
sources.notes: The 1 July 2024 official ministerial order establishes a prior visa requirement for nationals of the People's Republic of China, with an exception for public, official or diplomatic passports and applicable bilateral visa-exemption agreements; it does not provide a separate tourist result for Hong Kong or Macao SAR passports.

sources.authority: Embassy of the Republic of Paraguay in Japan
sources.title: Visa
sources.notes: The official embassy page lists countries exempt for short visits up to 90 days, states that countries not listed must obtain a visa before travel, and identifies the People's Republic of China, Hong Kong and Macao in the consular application requirements.

sources.title: Visa Grupos 1-2-3
sources.notes: The official embassy page places CHINA, including Hong Kong, Taiwan and Macao, in Tourist Visa Group II and lists the application form, flight details, accommodation or invitation, bank statements, yellow-fever certificate, six-month passport validity, photographs and consular appointment process. The page does not state a Group II stay period.

sources.authority: Dirección General de Migración y Extranjería, Costa Rica
sources.title: Visas
sources.notes: The official immigration page explains that Costa Rica's General Visa Guidelines determine visa requirements, exemptions and entry requirements by foreign nationality, and links the November 2025 official Directriz PDF. The reviewed page does not expose a target-document-specific final result.
